portfolio.title: EOC Buff // End of Campaign Report Generator
portfolio.summary: Full-stack client/server operational utility that ingests campaign data from Google Sheets via an authenticated local Python CORS proxy and renders styled Excel summaries with zero manual formula entry.
portfolio.context: Campaign reporting teams had to manually copy, reformat, and calculate performance metrics from live Google Sheets into client-facing Excel spreadsheets, risking human error and spending hours per reporting cycle.
portfolio.objective: Build a secure, lightweight, and self-contained reporting application that automatically pulls data, runs aggregation logic, and outputs formatted Excel reports.
portfolio.role: Lead Developer & Systems Architect — designed the architecture, wrote the Python proxy server, and engineered the browser-based data processing UI.
approach: Engineered a lightweight local HTTP proxy in Python (`server.py`) using `http.server` and `urllib.request` with domain-filtering safeguards (restricting requests strictly to `docs.google.com`) to bypass browser CORS constraints.

Built an interactive single-page application (`EOC_Report_Generator.html`) incorporating SheetJS (`xlsx`) and ExcelJS to read, normalize, and construct customized workbook layouts with embedded styles.
Implemented clean command-line logging and real-time frontend status feedback for report generation progress.
deliverables: Python HTTP proxy server with domain validation security.
Interactive browser-based report generator with SheetJS & ExcelJS processing.
Direct one-click export of styled Excel workbooks.
portfolio.outcome: Eliminated manual spreadsheet transcription errors and streamlined campaign wrap-up reporting into an automated workflow executable with a single command (`python server.py`).

portfolio.title: ShelfIQ // Perishable Spoilage Prediction & Restock Decision System
portfolio.summary: Multi-engine Streamlit machine learning application that predicts cold-chain perishable spoilage risks and generates automated rescue-pricing actions for Philippine grocery MSMEs.
portfolio.context: Mid-sized grocers and chilled-goods distributors face significant revenue loss during El Niño heat waves and cold-chain transit delays because standard static inventory models cannot anticipate transit decay.
portfolio.objective: Build an end-to-end ML decision support application forecasting Remaining Useful Life (RUL) and triggering timely discount strategies before goods spoil.
portfolio.role: Machine Learning Engineer (Capstone Co-Developer) — developed the Spoilage Prediction Engine (pages/rul_model.py) using Random Forest classification, mapped feature importances, and built automated urgency-tier markdown rules.
approach: Trained a Random Forest Classifier on historical inventory logs and transit metrics (stock levels, days to sell, daily demand, lead times, sensitivity scores) to predict perishable batch spoilage.

Engineered dynamic inference comparing current inventory lots against remaining shelf-life days to segment stock into four action tiers (Final Markdown <24h, Priority Sell 1-2d, Early Markdown 3-5d, Watch 5+d).
Implemented automated rescue interventions including upcycle recommendations for produce/dairy and targeted discount ranges (5% to 50%) to accelerate demand prior to spoilage.
Integrated prediction outputs directly into the shared Streamlit application with interactive KPI metrics and downloadable CSV reports.
deliverables: Random Forest Remaining Useful Life (RUL) Spoilage Engine (pages/rul_model.py).
Dynamic urgency tier categorization and markdown rule generator.
Interactive Streamlit dashboard metrics and downloadable CSV reports.
portfolio.outcome: Successfully pitched and demonstrated to Uplift Code Camp evaluators as an end-to-end decision support tool bridging data science predictions with actionable store-level retail decisions.

portfolio.title: Match Link // Company Name Templater
portfolio.summary: FastAPI and Pandas web utility that normalizes corporate legal suffixes, strips non-alphanumeric noise, and dynamically generates tiered Excel lookup formulas (Left 25, 15, 10) for automated CRM and database reconciliation.
portfolio.context: Reconciling vendor, client, and lead lists across CRM platforms and accounting databases frequently fails exact matching due to inconsistent entity spellings (e.g., 'PTE. LTD.', 'LLC', 'Corp') and punctuation differences.
portfolio.objective: Create a fast, standalone desktop/browser application to ingest tabular data, automate legal suffix stripping, and calculate live Excel formula helper columns for multi-tiered lookup matching.
portfolio.role: Lead Developer & Maintainer — designed the FastAPI backend, normalization regex pipelines, OpenPyXL workbook formatting, and glassmorphism interface.
approach: Engineered suffix-normalization regular expressions mapping varied legal forms (P.T.E. L.T.D., PRIVATE LIMITED, etc.) to canonical tokens before stripping them down to alphanumeric match keys.
Calculated 1-based dynamic Excel column indices to generate formula strings (=LEFT(ColRow, N)) directly inside exported workbooks.
Constructed an asynchronous FastAPI backend paired with an accessible drag-and-drop and text-paste frontend.
deliverables: FastAPI backend with /api/parse-headers, /api/template, and /api/download endpoints.
Responsive single-page web UI with file drag-and-drop and multi-line paste support.
One-click Windows launcher (run.bat) and automated test suite (test_templater.py).
portfolio.outcome: Automated data-preparation tasks for list reconciliation, eliminating manual text-editing hours and standardizing lookup keys across operational databases.
